title: Pinocchio Finds Geppetto
text:
Pinocchio, the wooden puppet carved by the poor old woodworker Geppetto, had caused his father endless grief. He sold his schoolbook, ran off with a puppet theater, was cheated by a fox and a cat, and was turned into a donkey for running away to the Land of Toys. Meanwhile Geppetto, searching for his lost son, had set out to sea in a little boat and vanished.

At last Pinocchio, thrown into the sea, was swallowed by the Terrible Dogfish, a sea monster a kilometer long. Deep inside its belly he saw a faint light. There, at a table, sat an old man, white as snow, eating live fish. It was Geppetto, who had been swallowed two years before and had survived on the supplies of a ship the monster had also swallowed. Now the last candle was nearly burned out.

Pinocchio threw his arms around his father. While the old monster slept with its mouth open, he led Geppetto out along its tongue. Geppetto could not swim, so Pinocchio took him on his shoulders and swam with him toward land, until both were nearly exhausted and a friendly tuna carried them ashore.

From then on Pinocchio worked. For months he turned a water wheel for a farmer to earn a glass of milk a day for his frail father, and in the evenings he wove baskets. One morning he woke to find he was no longer a puppet but a real boy.
lesson: Children begin to grow up when they start caring for the parents who cared for them. That turn from receiving to giving is the real change.
source: Carlo Collodi, The Adventures of Pinocchio (Le avventure di Pinocchio), 1883, Chapters 35 to 36
